title: How Much Should You Save for Home Repairs and Maintenance (U.S. Homeowners Guide)
description: Budgeting for CapEx: Roofs, HVACs, and the '1% Rule'.
content:
The sticker price of your mortgage is just the entry fee to homeownership. The real cost includes the slow, invisible depreciation of every system in your house. Your roof is dying. Your water heater is rusting. Your HVAC is aging. These are not 'unexpected emergencies'; they are predictable liabilities with a due date. If you do not save for them monthly, you will be forced to finance them on credit cards when they break. This guide helps you calculate your 'True Cost of Ownership' and build a sinking fund to cover it.

Key Takeaways

  • The 1% Rule: A standard baseline is to save 1% to 2% of your home's value annually for maintenance. On a $400k home, save $4,000/year ($333/month).
  • CapEx vs. Repairs: Distinguish between small repairs (leaky faucet) and Capital Expenditures (New Roof). You must save for the CapEx items over 10-20 years.
  • Age Adjustments: Newer homes (<10 years) need less saving (~0.5%). Older homes (>30 years) need aggressive saving (~2-3%) as major systems fail.
  • Separate Account: Keep this money in a dedicated 'House' High-Yield Savings Account. Do not mix it with your vacation fund.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Labor costs for tradespeople (plumbers, electricians) in the US have risen 40% since 2020. A job that cost $500 in 2019 might cost $900 today. Your savings rate must reflect this inflation in the service sector.

The Lifespan Audit

Walk through your house and assign a 'Death Date' to big items.

1. The Roof

Cost: $15,000. Life: 20 Years.
Cost/Year: $750. Monthly: $62.

2. HVAC System

Cost: $8,000. Life: 15 Years.
Cost/Year: $533. Monthly: $45.

3. Water Heater

Cost: $2,000. Life: 10 Years.
Cost/Year: $200. Monthly: $17.

4. Appliances/Painting/Flooring

Estimated: $1,200/year ($100/month).

Total Sinking Fund: $224/month.
This is the minimum amount you must save just to keep the house standing.

Tactical Funding

  1. Day 1 Fund: When you buy a house, do not spend all your cash on the down payment. Keep $5,000-$10,000 in a repair fund immediately. Something will break in the first month.
  2. Automate the 'HOA Fee': Even if you don't have an HOA, pay yourself a phantom HOA fee of $300/mo into the repair fund.
  3. Warranty Warning: Home Warranties ($600/yr) are often scams that deny claims. Self-insuring (saving that $600) is mathematically superior.
  4. Upgrade vs. Maintenance: Do not raid the Maintenance Fund for cosmetic upgrades (Granite Counters). Renovations require a separate savings goal.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I use a HELOC?

For emergencies (tree on roof), yes. For maintenance (new carpet), no. Do not finance depreciating assets with 8% debt. Pay cash.

What if I have a condo?

You cover 'Walls-In'. The HOA covers the roof/exterior. You still need a fund for appliances and HVAC, plus a buffer for 'Special Assessments'.

Can I invest this money?

Keep it liquid (HYSA or Money Market). When the furnace dies in January, you need cash today, not stocks that might be down 10%.
